name: coder-one-tunable-v9-escalate
note: The whole tunable composition in a Terminal-Bench episode: task.profile routes the start (Codex on GPT-6 Luna for cheap, likely-easy tasks; lean Claude Code on Opus 5.5 for hard or long ones), deep Jev briefs it, control.monitor watches, verify.checks and verify.support judge the result, control.handoff escalates Luna to lean Opus on a stall, a failed check, a contradicted requirement, or no answer, and verify.repair runs once from the diagnostic packets. control.horizon sizes every dispatch from the task's own timeout. Both executors run the headless core system prompt with its protected sections, and Claude Code writes the five-minute prompt cache. v2: the briefing uses the coverage packer with Jev coverage judgments, and verify.repair runs only when a scenario observed a failure (trigger checked). v3: long tasks (over an hour) run the executor at xhigh effort instead of medium; on Terminal-Bench 4.0, lean Opus at medium stopped itself after 1 to 3 minutes of an 8-hour budget, and the leaderboard's Opus 5 rows gain 30 passes of 330 from medium to xhigh. v9: v3 with control.effort, built on v3 rather than v8 so that v2 (medium), v3 (xhigh), and v9 differ only in the effort a long task runs at. One Jev request asks six Nouls over the task and the files the workspace starts with; the weighted mean of the answers at or above the threshold runs the task at xhigh, and below it at medium. A task whose features are unknown runs at xhigh. The weights and threshold are fitted on the unused task pool, labeled from the Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard (see control.effort.fit), never on the scored Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks: faithful_reproduction and long_reasoning separate the labels on the development split, and the others weigh nothing. v9-escalate (#9571): v9 plus escalation on a failed check only. verify.self_report, verify.behavior, verify.optional_outputs, and verify.support_budget are v7's checks, so the trigger can see the failures v7's checks flag (14 of 27 graded TB4 failures, 1 of 34 passes). verify.repair is off, so escalation, not a repair, answers a failed check: in the first targeted trial (docs/terminal-bench/2026-09-24-escalation-on-failed-check.md), v9's repair made the flagged report agree with itself, the checks passed, the verifier still failed it, and escalation never fired. verify.second runs Codex on GPT-6 Astra on the task's original state when a scenario other than the self-report failed (check) or the executor reported that its result fails (self_report), never when the checks merely can't confirm the result, and never on a contradiction verify.support reads alone. The host checks both candidates and keeps the one whose checks fail less, then confirm more requirements; a tie keeps the first. The composition record gives each escalation's triggers by name, executor, outcome, cost, and time. On TB4, v4's Astra second executor recovered two tasks Opus had failed (docs/terminal-bench/tb4-results.md), but its unconfirmed trigger fired on most tasks; v2's escalation fired 0 times in 49 trials.
